page.layout: One page of running text: a continuous Latin commentary with Greek words. Running head at the top with the page number at top left. Below the text: a centred heading "Ad caput ἀπονοίας." followed by a centred reference "Pap. 19." and one paragraph with a large initial. No marginal notes and no footnotes.

main_text.l: vitij huius simplicitate, quàm illa iactatione peruersi, si
abundans opibus pauperem se neget, nobilis obseruans,
& potens infirmum, aut si se dissertus imperitum plane
infantem vocet. Παλαιστρᾶν[?] certum est de loco hic
esse accipiendum, vt Pars in gramineis exercet mem-
bra palaestris. Est autem commune poëtis, philoso-
phis, sophistis, hoplomachis, harmonicis, atque
aliis item, vt τὰ μελέται[?], sic etiam τὸ ἐπιδεικνύσθαι[?]
habent enim quique eorum suas ἐπιδείξεις & exer-
citationes: quod notum est ex Græcis scriptori-
bus. Ὁπλομάχοι sunt, qui sub campidoctore veris
armis certare discunt, aut ipsi qui docent: puto
enim vtrunque hac voce significari. vide Platonem
in Lachete. At vulgò inuentus non veris armis se
exercebat: sed tudibus, aut pilis præpilatis, quæ
dicuntur Græcis ἐσφαιρωμένα ἀκόντια. Xenophon
libro secundo Ἀναβάσεως de Phalino quodam ita scribens,
[illegible, ~20 letters] videtur innuere hoplomachos
ea ætate fuisse appellatos, etiam eos qui tacti-ci
Græcis proprie dicuntur. vide Vegetium.
Ad caput ἀπονοίας.
Pap. 19.
Ἡ δὲ ἀπόνοια ἐστιν [illegible, ~12 letters] τῶν ἔργων καὶ λό-γων. ] Definitio ista ἀπονοίας parum plena est
nam cum discrimen latum sit inter ἀναιδωλίαν[?], de
qua infrà est integrum caput, & ἀπὸ οἴας[?] nihil vi-
detur in hac definitione, quod non conueniat etiam
τῇ ἀναιδωλίᾳ. quid enim pudor aliud est quàm vi-

page.notes: Greek readings marked [?] or illegible are doubtful: the line "scribens, ..." (p. 172, line 18) is mostly unreadable on the scan, and the opening of the Greek in the large-initial paragraph is faint. The Greek words Παλαιστρᾶν, τὰ μελέται, τὸ ἐπιδεικνύσθαι, ἀναιδωλίαν and ἀπὸ οἴας are best readings. The paragraph ends mid-line with "vi-" and continues on the next page with "tiosæ". No catchword and no signature are printed.
